settings.name: OIDF_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE
settings.description: The profile this process runs under: development, or production, which is also what unset means

when_wrong.detail: Anything but development, in any case and trimmed, runs as production; rar-model alone reads development only when it is written exactly so (F-0160)

settings.name: OIDF_ACCEPTED_RISKS
settings.description: The risky switches this deployment accepts in production, comma-separated, each a risk id alone or with the last day it holds (expiry-log-mode@2026-12-31, UTC)

when_wrong.detail: An entry that is empty, not a risk this release knows, dated wrongly or past its date, repeated, or without the date a dated risk needs is not accepted, and the start-up audit lists it at WARN; under the production profile a switch that needs that risk then refuses its components

settings.name: jdk.internal.httpclient.disableHostnameVerification
settings.description: The JDK's own switch, never this repository's: set, it turns off the host name check of every java.net.http client in the JVM - PingFederate's and every component's - for the life of the JVM. The JDK reads it once, in jdk.internal.net.http.common.Utils (JDK 17 and 21): unset checks host names, empty or true turns the check off, any other value checks. The production profile forbids it with any value (F-0035, F-0195)

when_wrong.detail: Set under the production profile, with any value: every component is REFUSED and answers 503, ready is 503, and PingFederate's own endpoints keep serving. Remove -Djdk.internal.httpclient.disableHostnameVerification from the JVM's options
